official_measurement_examples.name: Three licensing tests
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England standing advice requires relevant protected-species licensing tests to be capable of being met; planning permission can exist but still be impossible to implement without a required wildlife licence.

official_measurement_examples.name: DLL availability
official_measurement_examples.fact: Great crested newt district level licensing only operates in specified scheme areas; the March 2026 update states there are currently no local-planning-authority-led DLL schemes.

official_measurement_examples.name: DLL sequence
official_measurement_examples.fact: The March 2026 developer guidance separates joining a DLL scheme, development consent, applying for the district licence, payment and approval to start work.

official_measurement_examples.name: Bat mitigation licence
official_measurement_examples.fact: Development work affecting bats may require a mitigation licence; survey licences and mitigation licences serve different purposes and must not be substituted.

official_measurement_examples.name: Survey licence update
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England updated bat survey class licences in March 2026 and reference-form guidance in June 2026, so licence type and version date must be retained.

official_measurement_examples.name: Badger class licences
official_measurement_examples.fact: 2026 badger class licences are purpose-specific and time-limited, such as forestry or drainage operations, and do not authorise unrelated development impacts.

official_measurement_examples.name: Bat reform transition
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England's 2026 bat licensing reform work describes reforms and evidence development; future reform intentions are not current blanket permissions.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Species survey evidence, planning permission, protected-species licence and approval to commence licensed works are separate stages.

core_rules: planning permission is not a protected species licence
a protected species licence is not planning permission
species survey evidence is not a licence decision
a bat survey class licence is not a bat mitigation licence
district level licensing availability must be checked for the actual scheme area
joining a DLL scheme is not approval to start work
DLL strategic mitigation does not remove unrelated protected-species duties
class licences are purpose-specific and must not be reused outside scope
time-limited 2026 class licences must retain validity dates
future licensing reform proposals are not current permissions
absence of a recorded species observation is not proof of species absence
licensing tests require proposal-specific evidence and cannot be inferred from proximity alone
protected-species evidence does not determine land ownership
species licence status does not reserve development capacity
no parcel species clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Natural England, GOV.UK and Natural England blog sources checked on 2026-07-26. March-June 2026 GCN/bat licensing updates, current class-licence scope and planning/licensing separation were preserved; no parcel species clearance was promoted.
